hero.titlePart1: An ERP project should never fail
hero.subtitle: CNPS payroll, SYSCOHADA financial statements, Mobile Money payments, patchy connectivity: that's where most ERP rollouts derail in West Africa, not in the software. AKILI Labs implements Odoo starting from that reality, from business scoping through go-live and beyond.

hubDiagram.ariaLabel: Odoo brings together CRM, Inventory, Accounting, and HR on a single platform

intro.title: Scattered tools cost more than a unified system
intro.paragraph1: Running a growing business with scattered tools (spreadsheets, a standalone accounting package, a CRM disconnected from the supply chain) costs time, money, and missed opportunities. And the first instinct — adopting a generic ERP — often fails on the same issues: a chart of accounts that ignores SYSCOHADA, payroll that knows neither CNPS nor CGRAE, payments that stop where Mobile Money begins.
intro.calloutTitle: The right ERP is the one that adapts to your reality, not the other way around.
intro.calloutText: Odoo, the world's most widely adopted open-source ERP suite (28+ million users in 180 countries), brings sales, purchasing, inventory, accounting, HR, and manufacturing together on a single platform. Its open architecture enables exactly the adaptations your context requires.
intro.paragraph2Rich: At AKILI Labs, we don't just install Odoo. We configure it, adapt it, and keep it running true to your African business reality: OHADA/SYSCOHADA context, local tax specifics, multilingual environments, and connectivity constraints.
intro.imageAlt: Before-and-after: an Excel sales-tracking sheet with a duplicate order and #N/A errors, alongside a WhatsApp thread where the warehouse reports the stock count is out of date, next to the Odoo apps menu (Sales, CRM, Inventory, Purchase, Accounting, Payroll) and order CDE-2026-341 reserving stock, generating the invoice, and posting the accounting entry

conformite.title: A compliant ERP proves itself in the financial statements, not in the brochure
conformite.paragraph1: Any integrator can install Odoo. The difference lies in the thousands of details that local context demands: a Balance Sheet and Income Statement in revised SYSCOHADA format, a TAFIRE your statutory auditor accepts, payslips that get CNPS and CGRAE contributions exactly right, VAT configured for the tax rules of each country of operation, Wave, Orange Money, or MTN MoMo receipts reconciled automatically in the accounts.
conformite.paragraph2: AKILI Labs has built specific expertise in configuring Odoo for the OHADA framework: it's the core of our practice, not a line item on the quote.
conformite.imageAlt: Customer invoice in Odoo accounting: entries posted to SYSCOHADA accounts 411, 701, and 4431 with 18% VAT, a balanced trial balance, payment matching reconciled against the bank statement, OHADA financial statements generated, and the DSF reporting package ready for the DGI

hostingSupport.title: Your ERP has to run every single day: we commit to it contractually
hostingSupport.supportParagraphRich: After go-live, your ERP is covered by a maintenance contract with contractual service commitments: blocking incidents handled within 2 to 24 hours depending on the tier, statutory payroll updates included, monthly TMA (application maintenance), and follow-up reviews. Three tiers adapt to how critical your operations are.
hostingSupport.imageAlt: Odoo instance monitoring: 99.95% uptime over 12 months against a contractual target of 99.5%, an incident detected and resolved in 31 minutes, and P1-to-P3 TMA tickets handled within contractual deadlines

intro.title: Digitizing without scoping just automates the chaos
intro.paragraph1: Across the UEMOA zone, the pressure to modernize is real: competitiveness, OHADA regulatory requirements, and the expectations of customers and regulators. But organizations that digitize process by process, tool by tool, without an overall vision, end up with the same result: a fragmented information system that is costly to maintain and reproduces the slowness of paper in digital form.
intro.calloutTitle: The causes of failure are rarely technological.
intro.calloutText: They are organizational: no mapping of the real processes, prioritization driven by technology trends, and underestimating team adoption.
intro.paragraph2: That's why AKILI Labs steps in before any tool is chosen: we audit the current state, build an IT Master Plan prioritized by impact and feasibility, then steer the rollout through to adoption — paperless workflows, process automation, IT governance.
intro.imageAlt: Before-and-after: a scanned handwritten purchase order stamped 'pending,' with an empty signature box because the signatory is away on assignment, and the follow-up email thread 'Re: Re: Re: approval?', next to the same process digitized, with every step timestamped from 09:02 to 09:15

gouvernance.title: Your data is an asset — and a legal responsibility
gouvernance.paragraph1: Going paperless shifts obligations, it doesn't remove them: customer, HR, and accounting records remain subject to statutory retention requirements, and personal data protection regulations now apply in most countries across the zone.
gouvernance.paragraph2: A serious digital transformation builds these requirements in from the design stage: who can access what, where data is hosted, how it is archived and for how long, and how traceability is guaranteed in the event of an audit or dispute.

responsable.title: AI under your control: data, models, decisions
responsable.intro: Adopting AI shifts responsibilities that no decision-maker can delegate: where does your data live? Does it train a third party's models? Who has the final say when the algorithm recommends declining a loan or rejecting a candidate? Serious AI makes these questions traceable — and their answers contractual.
responsable.pillar1Desc: Your data never trains a third-party model. On-premise, private cloud, or hybrid architectures: your sensitive data never leaves your zone of control.
responsable.pillar2Desc: Personal data protection aligned with local and sub-regional regulatory frameworks; financial regulators' requirements factored in for banking use cases (scoring, credit approval).
responsable.pillar3Desc: AI proposes, humans decide: validation loops on sensitive decisions (credit, HR, healthcare), recommendations that are traceable and explainable to the business.
responsable.pillar4Desc: Bias testing and business validation before any production release; drift monitoring and periodic retraining once in operation.

hero.titlePart1: A production release should never be
hero.subtitle: Shipping fast and shipping safely aren't opposing goals — it's the traditional approach that pits them against each other: manual deployments, end-of-project audits, vulnerabilities discovered in production. AKILI Labs automates and standardizes your CI/CD pipeline with security built into every step, from code to operations.

intro.title: Security bolted on at the end is a debt, not a protection
intro.paragraph1: In many organizations, shipping an application is still a high-risk exercise: manual deployments, environments that drift between development and production, fixes postponed because "it works." Every release becomes a dreaded event instead of a controlled non-event.
intro.calloutQuote: Vulnerabilities discovered in production cost the most.
intro.calloutText: DevSecOps catches them early — at design, in code, in tests — reducing remediation costs and strengthening the trust of clients and partners.
intro.paragraph2: AKILI Labs automates and standardizes your delivery chain end to end: continuous integration and deployment, containerization, infrastructure described as code, automated security analysis, and monitoring — for frequent, reproducible, auditable releases.

securite.title: Compliance is proven with logs, not with promises
securite.paragraph1: Containerizing applications, automating deployments, migrating to the cloud: every step of industrialization shifts security responsibilities. Who accesses production environments? Where do secrets live — passwords, keys, certificates? What happens when a critical fix needs to go out on a Friday night?
securite.paragraph2: A serious DevSecOps chain makes these questions traceable: every deployment is logged, every access is controlled, every environment can be rebuilt identically. For regulated organizations in the zone — banks, microfinance, insurance — this traceability isn't a nicety: regional regulators require demonstrable management of IT risk and business continuity.

intro.title: Your processes deserve better than a spreadsheet — and better than a project that derails
intro.paragraph1: On one side, the need is real: case approvals, production tracking, member management, route planning… when no off-the-shelf software covers your specific workflows, teams compensate — shared spreadsheets, re-keyed data, paper tracking. Data scatters and no one has the full picture.
intro.paragraph2: On the other, the wariness is legitimate: too many organizations in the region have experienced the custom project whose budget doubles, the application delivered late and never formally accepted, or the provider who walked away with the code.
intro.calloutQuote: Custom projects almost always derail for the same three reasons.
intro.calloutText: Scope that's never locked down, a tunnel effect with no intermediate deliveries, and code the client doesn't own. Our standards exist precisely to neutralize these three causes — and they're verifiable.
intro.paragraph3Rich: Our doctrine: standard wherever your need is standard — a proven ERP like Odoo will be faster and cheaper there — and custom only where your process sets you apart. During the free scoping session, we tell you honestly which case you're in.

hero.subtitle: Sales, cash registers, inventory, Mobile Money: every day of activity produces numbers no one has time to consolidate. AKILI Labs turns this scattered data into reliable dashboards, refreshed every morning, so you decide on what's real — not on last month's report.
hero.imageAlt: Multi-branch management committee dashboard: revenue, cash position, and margin by branch in FCFA, with a manager's mobile view showing the day's sales and a cash discrepancy alert

intro.title: The monthly report costs two days. And it's already outdated.
intro.paragraph1: In most companies in the region, decision-making relies on an exhausting ritual: at the end of every month, one trusted person collects files from the branches, copies out the ERP figures, reconciles discrepancies by hand, and formats a committee report. Two days of work, numbers that diverge depending on the source, and management discovering on the 5th of the month what happened three weeks earlier.
intro.paragraph2: Our approach: yesterday's numbers, available every morning. Consolidation becomes an overnight process, no longer a job.
intro.calloutText: The problem is almost never a lack of data. It's that it's asleep across five systems that don't talk to each other, and that the one person who knows how to piece it together will one day go on leave.
intro.imageAlt: Before and after: an Excel consolidation workbook riddled with #REF! errors and a WhatsApp conversation where branches send their numbers late, versus a group dashboard consolidated automatically every night, reconciled with accounting, with branch-level detail

pilotage.calloutText: A dashboard tells you where you stand. The next step is to anticipate: demand forecasting, anomaly detection, scoring. That's the territory of our Artificial Intelligence practice, which builds precisely on the data warehouse constructed here.

gouvernance.title: Why your revenue figure differs depending on who calculates it, and how we end that
gouvernance.paragraph1: “Net revenue,” “active customer,” “outstanding balance”: as long as every department has its own formula, meetings serve to reconcile numbers instead of making decisions. We write each definition once, with you, and the system then applies it everywhere: dashboards, exports, alerts.
gouvernance.paragraph2: Quality checks run every night with the data flows: duplicates, unclosed cash registers, incomplete entries become visible and fixable, instead of being discovered at year-end close.
gouvernance.imageAlt: Net revenue KPI record in the dictionary: definition spelled out in full, SQL query applied across all screens, traceability from source to dashboards, CFO as the owner, and the results of the overnight quality checks

reglementaire.title: The statements that aren't up for debate: on time, accurate, archived

items.question: What is an OHADA-compliant ERP?
items.answer: An OHADA-compliant ERP is an integrated management system that follows the OHADA chart of accounts, in force across 17 African countries including Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal. It automates accounting, revised SYSCOHADA financial statements, and local VAT, eliminating manual reprocessing that is often a source of errors.

items.question: Why choose Odoo for a business in West Africa?
items.answer: Odoo is the most widely adopted ERP in the UEMOA zone thanks to its modularity, competitive total cost of ownership, and ability to adapt to local specifics (OHADA, Ivorian labor law, UEMOA VAT). With over 28 million users worldwide, its ecosystem of certified local partners guarantees lasting support.

items.question: How long does an Odoo ERP integration project take?
items.answer: A first modular rollout (accounting + inventory) takes 3 to 6 months. A full scope covering HR, OHADA payroll, CRM, and purchasing requires 6 to 12 months, including training. Duration depends on source data quality, the availability of business teams, and the level of customization required.

items.question: What is the difference between Odoo Community and Odoo Enterprise?
items.answer: Odoo Community is open-source and free. Odoo Enterprise adds advanced modules (payroll, e-signature, multi-company consolidation), official support from Odoo S.A., guaranteed security updates, and native mobile apps. AKILI Labs recommends Enterprise for organizations with more than 20 users or complex HR and OHADA payroll needs.

items.question: How does data migration from a legacy system work?
items.answer: Migration follows 4 steps: audit and mapping of source data, cleansing and transformation into Odoo's format, loading into a test environment with business validation, then cutover to production. AKILI Labs favors progressive imports and cross-consistency checks to avoid data loss or duplicates.

items.question: Where should you start your digital transformation?
items.answer: Digital transformation starts with an audit of the current setup: process mapping, identification of friction points, and potential gains. AKILI Labs produces an IT Master Plan (Schéma Directeur Informatique) that prioritizes initiatives by business impact and feasibility, factoring in UEMOA budget constraints.

items.question: What is an EDM (Electronic Document Management) system?
items.answer: An EDM system digitizes, classifies, indexes, and controls access to company documents. It eliminates paper archives, speeds up document search, and secures data. In the UEMOA zone, it is especially useful for client, HR, and accounting files subject to legal retention obligations.

items.question: How do you choose an IT partner in West Africa?
items.answer: A good IT partner in West Africa must master the local context: OHADA regulations, variable connectivity, and budget constraints in XOF. Check references in your industry, post-deployment support capacity, local presence for on-site interventions, and the team's technical certifications.

items.question: What is BPM and what is it used for?
items.answer: BPM (Business Process Management) models, automates, and optimizes business processes. It maps workflows, identifies bottlenecks, and implements automated workflows: approvals, notifications, escalations. The result: faster, more traceable processes that depend less on key individuals.

items.question: How can AI help my business in Africa?
items.answer: AI creates value on concrete use cases: automated credit file analysis (−94% turnaround time observed at a UEMOA client bank), support chatbots in French and local languages, document OCR, inventory forecasting, and accounting anomaly detection. The starting point is always a measurable business problem.

items.question: What is a private LLM and why use one?
items.answer: A private LLM (Large Language Model) is an AI model deployed on your own infrastructure or a dedicated cloud, with no data shared with third parties. It guarantees the confidentiality of customer, HR, and financial data. AKILI Labs deploys solutions based on Ollama, LLaMA, or Mistral, hosted in your controlled environment.

items.question: What is RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)?
items.answer: RAG connects an AI model to your own data: internal documents, knowledge base, ERP. The AI first searches your sources, then generates an accurate, traceable answer without hallucination. It is the recommended method for deploying a reliable document assistant or business chatbot on private data.

items.question: Is generative AI secure for enterprise data?
items.answer: Generative AI is secure when properly architected. AKILI Labs recommends models deployed on-premises or in a dedicated VPC, with per-client isolation, request logging, and granular access control. Third-party cloud APIs (ChatGPT, Gemini) are not recommended for sensitive data without a prior risk analysis.

items.question: What is DevSecOps?
items.answer: DevSecOps embeds security at every stage of the software development lifecycle: design, code, testing, deployment, production. Unlike the traditional approach where security comes in at the end of a project, DevSecOps detects vulnerabilities early, reduces remediation costs, and strengthens trust with customers and partners.

items.question: Why containerize my applications with Docker?
items.answer: Docker packages an application with all its dependencies into a portable container. The result: identical environments from development to production, reproducible deployments, service isolation, and easier scaling. Paired with Kubernetes, it lets you manage dozens of services in an automated way, with 10× less deployment time.

items.question: What is Infrastructure as Code (IaC)?
items.answer: IaC consists of describing and provisioning your infrastructure (servers, networks, databases) through version-controlled code files (Terraform, Ansible). Your environments become reproducible, auditable, and deployable in minutes. DEV, QA, and PROD stay consistently aligned, eliminating bugs caused by configuration drift.

items.question: What is the difference between CI and CD?
items.answer: CI (Continuous Integration) automates testing and builds on every code commit: errors are detected in under 10 minutes. CD (Continuous Deployment) automatically pushes validated code to target environments. Together, CI/CD reduce delivery times from weeks to hours while maintaining quality.

items.question: Which countries does AKILI Labs operate in?
items.answer: AKILI Labs operates in the 8 countries of the UEMOA zone: Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Togo, Benin, and Guinea-Bissau. Our headquarters is in Abidjan. For remote projects, we operate across the entire ECOWAS zone and also support French organizations with subsidiaries in West Africa.

items.question: How do I start a project with AKILI Labs?
items.answer: Three steps: (1) Contact us by email or online form, with a response within 24 business hours. (2) A free scoping consultation: we analyze your needs, context, and budget constraints. (3) A technical and financial proposal within 5 business days. No commitment on your part before you approve the proposal.

items.question: Do you offer TMA (application maintenance) services?
items.answer: Yes. AKILI Labs provides ongoing TMA for your systems with contractual SLAs: P1 incidents resolved within 4h, P2 within 24h. Our TMA contracts include proactive monitoring, security updates, Odoo patches, minor enhancements, and a dedicated project manager. P1 SLA compliance rate: 100% over the past 12 months.

items.question: What is your pricing approach?
items.answer: Our services are offered on a time-and-materials basis (daily rate) or as a fixed-price package. For ERP projects, we offer CAPEX (upfront investment) or OPEX (monthly subscription) plans suited to the cash-flow constraints of UEMOA organizations. The initial consultation is free and non-binding. Quotes within 5 business days.
